The proximate cause here seems to be fvar's use of
boost::math::isnan() to set the tangent to NaN. But
it would probably creep in elsewhere, because I don't see
why that one's special. I was hoping we could just get rid
of the problem, which we may be able to do by not using
Boost's isnan anywhere. I'm getting lost in all the refactoring,
but my understanding was that we were going to get rid of
Boost's isnan() and use our own.

Ben, if including this in var.hpp with no #ifdef
var(__float128 x) : vi_(new vari(static_cast<double>(x))) { }

lets you compile, can you try this:

#ifdef BOOST_MATH_USE_FLOAT128

var(__float128 x) : vi_(new vari(static_cast<double>(x))) { }
#endif

That may introduce an order dependency, and if it doesn't work,
maybe a spell-corrected version of my first attempt would work (I forgot
the final "__" on "__GNUC_MINOR__"):

#if (__GNUC__ > 4) || ((__GNUC__ == 4) && (__GNUC_MINOR__ >= 3))

var(__float128 x) : vi_(new vari(static_cast<double>(x))) { }
#endif

That should not depend on Boost --- if we use the Boost property,
then we may have more ordering issues.


The offending bit of Boost code that enables the non-standard
type __float128 is here:

lib/boost_1.55.0//boost/math/tools/config.hpp

which has:

#if defined(_GLIBCXX_USE_FLOAT128) && defined(BOOST_GCC) && !defined(__STRICT_ANSI__)
//
// Only enable this when the compiler really is GCC as clang and probably
// intel too don't support __float128 yet :-(
//
# define BOOST_MATH_USE_FLOAT128
#endif


I'd go back to trying enable_if, but I couldn't get it to work on
Windows --- the tests all passed here and crashed and burned on Jenkins.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] test __float128 patch?
parts:
So... Bob, I think you should add your patch.

But I also think that the test is missing includes for digamma, based on how it's being used. I'll go ahead and add some includes and submit a pull request.


Daniel

On Thu, Mar 12, 2015 at 12:07 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:



> On Mar 13, 2015, at 2:39 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
>
> Thanks, Bob.
>
> could source of the problem be stan/math/rev/scal/fun/lgamma.hpp? It calls boost directly.

Yes, that's how we compute gamma and digamma.

The <valarray> and <...constants.hpp> includes seem unnecessary.

I'm not even sure what you mean by "source of the problem."
Can you compile and test lgamma?  If so, then it's not by itself
the source of the problem.

I also thought it was the forward version acting up?

That itself also brings in way more than necessary with all of
fwd/core.hpp.

- Bob


>
> On Mar 12, 2015 10:32 AM, "Bob Carpenter" <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> We definitely need the digamma for derivatives of
> the gamma function.  It's also a pain for higher-order
> derivatives, because you then need trigramma, and then
> I'm not sure what for third order derivatives.
>
> My question is whether lkj_corr needed it.  I guess
> it does because it uses beta distributions and they
> implicate gamma, which in turn implicates digamma.
>
> - Bob
>
> > On Mar 13, 2015, at 1:30 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> >
> > It looks like it's necessary.
> >
> > I'll try to find out what part of boost calls it. It's getting implicitly instantiated somehow, so we need this digamma function, I'm just not sure where.
> >
> > On Thu, Mar 12, 2015 at 10:24 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> > I'll just set develop back to where it was.
> >
> > You're absolutely right on the digamma comment. I'm now trying to hunt down which piece of that will make this function work.
> >
> > On Thu, Mar 12, 2015 at 10:18 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> > Well, feel free to do what you want with my messed up
> > git merge.  Was that why you were asking the last question?
> >
> > Why do you want to include digamma in lkj_corr?  That seems
> > like the wrong fix unless it uses the function.
> >
> > - Bob
> >
> > > On Mar 13, 2015, at 1:14 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> > >
> > > Ok. Found it!
> > >
> > > Ben, can you include this header:
> > > #include <stan/math/rev/scal/fun/digamma.hpp>
> > >
> > > right before the include to lkj_corr? It doesn't need to be right there, but that seems to work just fine. I also put it closer to the top and it works.
> > >
> > >
> > > Bob, if this works, I think we should fix it by including this into the test rather than macros for the includes. This is really just a mix autodiff problem, forward and backwards interacting together.
> > >
> > > On Thu, Mar 12, 2015 at 10:03 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> > > Ok... I narrowed it down to need a header inside <stan/math/rev/scal.hpp>.
> > >
> > > (I thought it'd be in mat, but what do I know? template metaprogramming is tricky. I'll let you know exactly which header we needed to include.)
> > >
> > > On Thu, Mar 12, 2015 at 9:38 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> > > That's very weird.  I'm wondering if there's something
> > > odd going on where we would accidentally call the __float128
> > > type?
> > >
> > > I also wonder why it's just lkj_corr that's causing issues.
> > >
> > > - Bob
> > >
> > >
> > > > On Mar 13, 2015, at 12:33 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
> > > >
> > > > Bob, I was able to set up a virtual machine with g++ 4.9.
> > > >
> > > > The weird thing is that the patch isn't needed if we #include <stan/model/model_header.hpp> right before including <stan/math/prim/mat/prob/lkj_corr.hpp>
> > > >
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Thu, Mar 12, 2015 at 9:30 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> > > > Thanks! I'll put in the patch and make sure to deal
> > > > with the order dependency properly.
> > > >
> > > > - Bob
> > > >
> > > > > On Mar 13, 2015, at 12:17 AM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > >
> > > > > On Thursday, March 12, 2015 at 4:49:18 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> > > > > Ben, if including this in var.hpp with no #ifdef
> > > > >
> > > > >       var(__float128 x) : vi_(new vari(static_cast<double>(x))) { }
> > > > >
> > > > > lets you compile,
> > > > >
> > > > > Yes, that works.
> > > > >
> > > > > can you try this:
> > > > >
> > > > > #ifdef BOOST_MATH_USE_FLOAT128
> > > > >       var(__float128 x) : vi_(new vari(static_cast<double>(x))) { }
> > > > > #endif
> > > > >
> > > > > That also works.
> > > > >
> > > > > That may introduce an order dependency, and if it doesn't work,
> > > > > maybe a spell-corrected version of my first attempt would work (I forgot
> > > > > the final "__" on "__GNUC_MINOR__"):
> > > > >
> > > > > #if (__GNUC__ > 4) || ((__GNUC__ == 4) && (__GNUC_MINOR__ >= 3))
> > > > >       var(__float128 x) : vi_(new vari(static_cast<double>(x))) { }
> > > > > #endif
> > > > >
> > > > > That didn't work.
> > > > >
> > > > > Ben
